  1. net.phoenix.chromatic_codes.api

Troubleshooting

Start with the symptom below. Check the call or file that produced the result, inspect its reported failure and apply the matching correction before retrying.

My code appears as ordinary text

Start with the code and its registration:

  • Check the code form. Bracket tokens need their closing bracket, and full hex tokens require all six marked digits.
  • Check the trigger and its case. Names are case-sensitive by default. Character triggers cannot replace reserved vanilla codes.
  • Inline definitions must be enabled and use a registered movement. Check the inline definition rules.

The mod drawing the text must use Minecraft's FontRenderer. A custom renderer may bypass these hooks. Some text fields also strip formatting codes before they reach the renderer; those fields keep their own input rules.

My edited configuration does not apply

Reload resources and look for Cannot apply text settings from in the client log. The message names the file; the accompanying exception explains the failure. Fix the reported problem, save any edits and reload resources again.

Rejected input keeps the previous settings active and leaves your file unchanged. The new definitions apply only when the whole configuration is valid. Hex colors in configuration palettes need six digits; inline palettes also accept three. Check the category and list structure, duplicate triggers, supported option names and numeric ranges.

If the first load fails, this file's presets have not been installed. The standalone client creates a default file only when chromatic_codes.cfg is missing; it leaves an existing invalid file for you to correct.

If another mod calls useExternalConfiguration(), the standalone listener stops applying chromatic_codes.cfg. That mod is responsible for reading its file and passing a Settings record to apply. The switch alone leaves the current definitions active. Edit that mod's file and use its reload mechanism; see host-managed configuration.

An effect looks different than I expected

Movement controls have effect-specific meanings. For size, moveSpeed is a scale; for spacing, it is an advance cushion; for 3d, the original constructor control is a layer count. Independent animationSpeed changes playback without changing geometry. Use explicit options for total extrusion depth/direction. Whole-segment transforms keep nominal flow width, so a visually larger breathing word does not push its neighbor back and forth.

Font resources determine which glyphs are available. Resource packs that omit requested Matrix alphabet characters can change its appearance. No replacement font or atlas-filtering override is installed.

If the change appears after wrapping or reverse trimming, check whether a custom color was applied after the effect. Rebuilt prefixes can lose that color while retaining the effect. This matters when the effect uses the incoming text color; see the formatting and continuation rules.

The mod fails to load

Use Minecraft 1.12.2 with the declared Cleanroom/Java requirements and Forgelin Continuous. Install the production JAR, not the mapped developer JAR. Remove duplicate embedded providers only after the host has been migrated to the external dependency. Do not register this mod's FontRenderer mixin a second time. Preserve the full failure log when reporting a compatibility issue.

When you finish: If a registration fails, keep the previous valid set active while correcting the input. Close only the receipts or movement scopes your addon owns. Restore a temporary TextEffectClock scope when a preview finishes.
